key_insight: Large language models can use their internal (parametric) knowledge to verify factual claims directly, enabling reliable fact checking without relying on external retrieval. This reduces dependency on noisy or unavailable evidence sources while maintaining competitive verification performance.
problem_solved: Removes the need for retrieval-based evidence pipelines that introduce errors, latency, and brittleness when checking the factuality of natural language claims.
method: Formulate claim verification as a direct LLM prompting/fine-tuning task that asks the model to judge and justify a claim using its parametric knowledge.
Apply calibration and consistency techniques (e.g., few-shot prompts, structured answer formats, confidence scoring) to improve reliability and reduce hallucination.
Compare and validate the retrieval-free approach against retrieval-based baselines across standard fact-checking/evaluation datasets and scenarios.
impact: Simplifies fact-checking systems by removing external retrieval dependencies, lowering latency and engineering complexity while improving robustness when evidence is missing or inaccessible. Practitioners can deploy lighter, faster verification components for safer agentic AI.

paper_title: Leveraging LLM Parametric Knowledge for Fact Checking without Retrieval
paper_authors: Artem Vazhentsev, Maria Marina, Daniil Moskovskiy, Sergey Pletenev, Mikhail Seleznyov
